MATHEMATICS — MOCK EXAM #12
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which digit holds a place in 6,092 even though it is worth nothing? (1 mark)
   A. 2
   B. 6
   C. 0
   D. 9

2. What is the total value of the digit 3 in 5,306? (1 mark)
   A. 3
   B. 30
   C. 300
   D. 3,000

3. Which is the smallest number: 819, 891, 189, 918? (1 mark)
   A. 918
   B. 819
   C. 189
   D. 891

4. How many factors does 20 have? (1 mark)
   A. 5
   B. 6
   C. 8
   D. 7

5. What is 450 ÷ 100? (1 mark)
   A. 45
   B. 5 remainder 50
   C. 4 remainder 5
   D. 4 remainder 50

6. Which division fact belongs to the same family as 8 × 3 = 24? (1 mark)
   A. 3 ÷ 8 = 24
   B. 24 ÷ 8 = 3
   C. 24 ÷ 8 = 8
   D. 24 ÷ 24 = 8

7. What is 48 ÷ 4? (1 mark)
   A. 11
   B. 12
   C. 22
   D. 13

8. What is 2/5 of 30? (1 mark)
   A. 18
   B. 6
   C. 12
   D. 7

9. Ali writes some fractions. Which of these is a proper fraction? (1 mark)
   A. 3/8
   B. 1 3/4
   C. 11/5
   D. 7/4

10. Why must the parts be equal when we write the fraction 1/3? (1 mark)
   A. The whole is cut into three parts of the same size
   B. Only the shaded part must be equal
   C. The numerator must be 3
   D. The parts can be any size

11. What is 1/4 of 36? (1 mark)
   A. 5
   B. 18
   C. 9
   D. 27

12. Which is the smallest number: 0.3, 0.29, 0.31, 0.03? (1 mark)
   A. 0.3
   B. 0.03
   C. 0.31
   D. 0.29

13. A stick is 1.5 m long. How many centimetres is that? (1 mark)
   A. 105 cm
   B. 150 cm
   C. 1,500 cm
   D. 15 cm

14. A hundred square has 35 of its small squares shaded. Which decimal shows the shaded part? (1 mark)
   A. 0.35
   B. 0.035
   C. 3.5
   D. 35

15. If y = 3, what is the value of 8 − y? (1 mark)
   A. 11
   B. 5
   C. 83
   D. 24

16. What is 1.2 m in centimetres? (1 mark)
   A. 102 cm
   B. 1,200 cm
   C. 12 cm
   D. 120 cm

17. A square has sides of 15 m. What is its perimeter? (1 mark)
   A. 225 m
   B. 30 m
   C. 60 m
   D. 45 m

18. A fence uses 4 pieces of wire, each 2 m 30 cm long. What is the total length of wire? (1 mark)
   A. 10 m 20 cm
   B. 9 m 10 cm
   C. 2 m 34 cm
   D. 9 m 20 cm

19. Change 908 cm to metres and centimetres. (1 mark)
   A. 9 m 58 cm
   B. 9 m 8 cm
   C. 90 cm
   D. 10 m 8 cm

20. A floor is covered with square tiles in 8 rows of 12 tiles. How many tiles are on the floor? (1 mark)
   A. 86 tiles
   B. 96 tiles
   C. 20 tiles
   D. 104 tiles

21. What is 5 1/4 L + 2 1/4 L? (1 mark)
   A. 7 3/4 L
   B. 7 1/2 L
   C. 7 1/4 L
   D. 8 L

22. How long is a lesson that starts at 8:15 a.m. and ends at 10:40 a.m.? (1 mark)
   A. 2 h 25 min
   B. 3 h 25 min
   C. 2 h 10 min
   D. 2 h 35 min

23. Change 96 hours to days. (1 mark)
   A. 5 days
   B. 1.6 days
   C. 8 days
   D. 4 days

24. Assembly starts at eight o'clock in the morning. How do we write this time? (1 mark)
   A. 8:00 p.m.
   B. 8:00 a.m.
   C. 8:00 noon
   D. 8:30 a.m.

25. A film starts at 4:20 p.m. and lasts 1 hour 40 minutes. At what time does it end? (1 mark)
   A. 6:00 p.m.
   B. 6:20 p.m.
   C. 5:60 p.m.
   D. 5:40 p.m.

26. A customer pays with Ksh 1,000 for goods that cost Ksh 750. How much change should she get? (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 1,750
   B. Ksh 350
   C. Ksh 250
   D. Ksh 240

27. A gate opens through a quarter turn from the wall. What angle does it make with the wall? (1 mark)
   A. A full turn
   B. No angle
   C. A right angle
   D. A straight line

28. Which shape has no corners? (1 mark)
   A. Rectangle
   B. Square
   C. Triangle
   D. Circle

29. The table shows the pets kept by 10 families: dog 3, cat 3, rabbit 2, hen 2. What is the total of all the numbers? (1 mark)
   A. 11
   B. 10
   C. 9
   D. 12

30. In a tally chart, one group of five and 1 more single tally mark are drawn. What number do they show? (1 mark)
   A. 11
   B. 5
   C. 6
   D. 7

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Find the volume of a cube with sides of 4 blocks. (3 marks)

32. Write the next three numbers in the pattern 5, 9, 13, 17, ... and state the rule. (3 marks)

33. A buyer picks biscuits at Ksh 50, juice at Ksh 80 and a book at Ksh 120. He pays with a Ksh 500 note. Find the total cost and his change. (4 marks)

34. A tally chart shows walking 6, bicycle 2, bus 1 and car 1 for 10 pupils. How many pupils walk to school? How many do not walk? (3 marks)

35. Change 2 1/3 and 1 5/6 to improper fractions. (4 marks)

36. Otieno is a years old and his sister is 3 years older. Write an expression for his sister's age and find her age if Otieno is 9. (3 marks)

37. A bus carried 5,684 passengers on Saturday and 3,749 on Sunday. Find the total number of passengers and check your answer by adding in the opposite order. (4 marks)

38. Tabitha cuts a 7 m 20 cm rope into 6 pieces of equal length. Find the length of one piece. (3 marks)

39. Explain the difference between area and volume. (2 marks)

40. Why can we not tell the mass of an object only by looking at its size? Give an example. (3 marks)

41. Explain what the 0 in 4.05 shows and say how 4.05 is different from 4.5. (3 marks)

42. Find 3/4 of 12 counters. Explain each step. (3 marks)

43. A hall floor is covered with 12 rows of 15 square tiles. (a) How many tiles cover the floor? (b) A smaller room has 9 rows of 12 tiles. How many more tiles does the hall need than the smaller room? (5 marks)

44. A rectangular field is 45 m long and 30 m wide. (a) Find its perimeter. (b) A farmer wants to fence it but leaves two gates of 3 m each. How many metres of fence does he need? (5 marks)

45. Change 3 hours to minutes and 2 days to hours. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — MOCK EXAM #12 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — 0
   The zero shows that there are no hundreds. Without it the number would be 692.

2. C — 300
   The digit 3 is in the hundreds place, so its total value is 3 × 100 = 300.

3. C — 189
   Compare the digits from the left. The smallest number is 189.

4. B — 6
   The factors of 20 are 1, 2, 4, 5, 10, 20. There are 6 of them.

5. D — 4 remainder 50
   4 × 100 = 400 and 450 − 400 = 50. So 450 ÷ 100 = 4 remainder 50.

6. B — 24 ÷ 8 = 3
   Division undoes multiplication. Since 8 × 3 = 24, we know 24 ÷ 8 = 3 and 24 ÷ 3 = 8.

7. B — 12
   4 × 12 = 48, so 48 ÷ 4 = 12.

8. C — 12
   30 ÷ 5 = 6 and 6 × 2 = 12. So 2/5 of 30 is 12.

9. A — 3/8
   In a proper fraction the numerator is smaller than the denominator, so 3/8 is less than one whole.

10. A — The whole is cut into three parts of the same size
   A fraction shows equal parts of a whole. If the parts are different sizes, one part is not one third.

11. C — 9
   36 ÷ 4 = 9 and 9 × 1 = 9. So 1/4 of 36 is 9.

12. B — 0.03
   Give every number the same number of decimal places and compare from the left. The smallest number is 0.03.

13. B — 150 cm
   0.5 m = 50 cm, so 1.5 m = 100 cm + 50 cm = 150 cm.

14. A — 0.35
   35 out of 100 squares is 35/100 = 0.35.

15. B — 5
   Replace the letter by its value and work it out. The answer is 5.

16. D — 120 cm
   1 m = 100 cm. Use this to change between the two units: 1.2 m in centimetres is 120 cm.

17. C — 60 m
   A square has four equal sides. 15 + 15 + 15 + 15 = 60.

18. D — 9 m 20 cm
   230 × 4 = 920 cm = 9 m 20 cm.

19. B — 9 m 8 cm
   908 ÷ 100 = 9 remainder 8. So 908 cm = 9 m 8 cm.

20. B — 96 tiles
   8 × 12 = 96 tiles.

21. B — 7 1/2 L
   Work with the whole litres first and then the parts. 5 1/4 L + 2 1/4 L = 7 1/2 L.

22. A — 2 h 25 min
   Count on from 8:15 a.m. to 10:40 a.m.. The total is 2 h 25 min.

23. D — 4 days
   96 ÷ 24 = 4 days.

24. B — 8:00 a.m.
   Times from midnight to noon use a.m. and times from noon to midnight use p.m. The correct answer is 8:00 a.m..

25. A — 6:00 p.m.
   4:20 + 1 hour = 5:20 and 5:20 + 40 minutes = 6:00 p.m.

26. C — Ksh 250
   Change = amount paid − cost = 1,000 − 750 = Ksh 250.

27. C — A right angle
   A quarter turn makes a right angle.

28. D — Circle
   A circle has one curved edge and no corners.

29. B — 10
   Add all the numbers: 3 + 3 + 2 + 2 = 10.

30. C — 6
   1 × 5 + 1 = 6.

SECTION B
----
31. (3 marks)
   Answer: 64 blocks
   Working / marking points: 4 × 4 = 16 per layer (1 mark); 16 × 4 (1 mark); 64 blocks (1 mark).

32. (3 marks)
   Answer: Rule: add 4. Next numbers: 21, 25, 29.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the rule and 2 marks for the three correct numbers (1 mark if only two are correct).

33. (4 marks)
   Answer: Total Ksh 250; change Ksh 250
   Working / marking points: 50 + 80 + 120 = 250 (2 marks); 500 − 250 = 250 (2 marks).

34. (3 marks)
   Answer: 6 pupils walk. 10 − 6 = 4 pupils do not walk.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 6, 1 mark for 10 − 6, 1 mark for 4.

35. (4 marks)
   Answer: 7/3 and 11/6
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for 2 × 3 + 1 = 7 so 7/3; 2 marks for 1 × 6 + 5 = 11 so 11/6.

36. (3 marks)
   Answer: a + 3. When a = 9, her age is 12 years.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a + 3, 1 mark for replacing a by 9, 1 mark for 12 years.

37. (4 marks)
   Answer: 9,433 passengers. Check: 3,749 + 5,684 = 9,433.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for correct working with regrouping, 1 mark for the answer with unit, 1 mark for the check.

38. (3 marks)
   Answer: 1 m 20 cm
   Working / marking points: 720 ÷ 6 = 120 cm (2 marks); 120 cm = 1 m 20 cm (1 mark).

39. (2 marks)
   Answer: Area is the amount of flat surface a shape covers, in square units. Volume is the amount of space a solid takes up, in cubic units.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for area and 1 mark for volume.

40. (3 marks)
   Answer: A large sponge is light but a small stone is heavy. Mass depends on what the object is made of, so we must measure it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for saying size does not decide mass, 1 mark for an example, 1 mark for saying we must measure.

41. (3 marks)
   Answer: The 0 shows that there are no tenths. 4.05 is 4 ones and 5 hundredths; 4.5 is 4 ones and 5 tenths, which is bigger.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the meaning of zero, 1 mark for each correct reading.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: 9 counters. 12 ÷ 4 = 3 counters in one quarter; 3 × 3 = 9.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for dividing by the denominator, 1 mark for multiplying by the numerator, 1 mark for the answer.

43. (5 marks)
   Answer: (a) 180 tiles (b) 72 more tiles
   Working / marking points: (a) 12 × 15: 12 × 10 = 120 and 12 × 5 = 60, so 180 (2 marks); smaller room 9 × 12 = 108 (1 mark); 180 − 108 (1 mark); 72 tiles (1 mark).

44. (5 marks)
   Answer: (a) 150 m (b) 144 m
   Working / marking points: (a) 45 + 30 + 45 + 30 = 150 m (2 marks for method, 1 mark for the answer with unit); (b) 2 × 3 = 6 m and 150 − 6 = 144 m (2 marks total, awarded 1 for 6 m and 1 for 144 m). Total 5 marks.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: 180 minutes and 48 hours
   Working / marking points: 3 × 60 = 180 (1 mark); 2 × 24 = 48 (1 mark).
